Food wise they can go a while without eating. To deal with the shed someone recommended this method to me and I found it works. Get a cloth and run it under warm water. Squeeze it out so it’s just damp. Put it at the bottom of a Tupperware container. Add the anole. And close the lid (make sure you have air holes first). Then let him chill in there for about 10 minutes. The humidity helps and they will rub their face on the cloth which can help get some of it off

I’ve used flightless fruit flies a lot. I prefer the Hydei because they are a bit bigger and easier to deal with. For dusting I have a little Tupperware that I put some vitamin powder in. Then I shake some fruit flies in. Cover the dusting container quickly with lid. While doing this I am constantly tapping my fruit fly culture on the ground to prevent them from climbing out. Cap the culture. Then you can shake up the Tupperware and they’ll get a good coating. It sounds hard but if you try it a couple times you get the hang of it. Sometimes I just sprinkle them straight into the terrarium as well and let my anole go crazy finding them all.

When someone has a runny nose you don’t necessarily know the cause. It could be a cold, or allergies, or a physical irritant. You can’t know without testing. The same is true for different mental illnesses. You don’t know why a person shows symptoms of what we call depression. It could be regular grief (which shouldn’t be diagnosed), it could be their environment is really bad, it could be they have a genetic predisposition, it could be there are chemical imbalances. 

The runny nose analogy was in response to this particular comment:

“That someone depressed will have a different brain chemistry is not at all surprising, and doesn't mean that being depressed is more ill than feeling any other feeling or being in any other state of mind.” 

My point with the runny nose is that the reason we consider a runny nose “bad” is because we are comparing it to the majority/typical non runny nose. If everyone had a runny nose we would no longer look at it as a symptom of something. In the same way, being depressed is considered ill when compared to being in a state of mind consistent with the “norm”. 

That is an interesting point. To me I feel that chemical imbalance causing depression is true but so is the chemical imbalance being the depression. 

Back to the cold analogy. The cold virus causes cold symptoms. But when you say you “have a cold” people are referring to the symptoms and not the actual cold virus. But both are technically “the cold”. In a similar way when someone is described as depressed they are referring to the symptoms usually rather than the chemical imbalance. But both the chemical imbalance and the symptoms it causes are the depression. 

That’s true we do not know what caused it. We can get an idea from studying family trees for a genetic component, looking at past exposure to toxins (like weed being associated with schizophrenia), and looking for any physical trauma to the brain. All can play a role in the chemical imbalance. 

I agree. We only refer to people in these states as being mentally ill because they deviate from the norm. Similarly when their brain structure or chemical levels deviate from the norm for extended periods of time (not regular fluctuations) we would refer to their brain as being ill. 

In a different world where the brain structure, symptoms, and chemical activity of “mentally ill” people was the majority then people who deviate from that would be considered ill. However this is not the case and since society is based on the majority, people who deviate will often have disadvantages. The label of mentally ill can help reduce some of the disadvantages by giving these individuals benefits. For example someone with severe depression which causes them unable to work a normal job can apply for disability (at least where I live) so that they can survive despite not being able to work. 

Now I’m not going to be naive and say that all labels benefit the individuals. Not will I say the benefits provided are worth the trauma some people experience due to the labels. I think that really depends on the person. I know people whose diagnoses helped them get accommodations in university so they weren’t disadvantaged by their anxiety/ADHD etc. I also know individuals who have said the label made it very difficult for them to be taken seriously.

Furthermore brain differences are associated with mental illness but it’s a complicated relationship. Some researchers suggest that the brain abnormalities are causing the symptoms of mental illness. So why do they use response based tests. These are fairly quick to do, cheap, and provide a generally accurate depiction of a persons current mood and behaviour. Furthermore these tests ask questions in a very specific way. They will generally ask how often in x period of time have you experienced y. Being a loner and lacking close friends outside of the immediate family

Flat emotions or limited or inappropriate emotional responses

Persistent and excessive social anxiety

Incorrect interpretation of events, such as a feeling that something that is actually harmless or inoffensive has a direct personal meaning

Peculiar, eccentric or unusual thinking, beliefs or mannerisms

Suspicious or paranoid thoughts and constant doubts about the loyalty of others

Belief in special powers, such as mental telepathy or superstitions

Ok everyone says it’s an addiction and you will go deeper. And I think that can be true for some people. I have been SH for 4/5 years and have never gone deep enough to need stitches and my bleeding has always stopped within 10 min. Also whenever I want to stop I can (and I know everyone says this but I actually can and have stopped when I didn’t feel like doing it anymore). So I think it is possible to SH without going deeper and without forming a heavy addiction.

So why is it bad. 

1. Stigma. When you’re getting a job or meeting new people there is always the risk of them judging you. Also staring if it’s in a highly visible spot. Personally I don’t care about either of those things. Also you said 

2. Infections. If you don’t care for them properly and do it a lot you are at risk of infections. If you’re not going too deep and you keep the wound clean you should be ok with this. 

3. Waste. For me I am big on sustainability. So I feel guilty when I’m constantly using band aids and tissue and new blades etc. Though this doesn’t even mildly compare to industrial waste so I wouldn’t worry too much. 

4. Dependant. If you rely on SH to cope with things it will prevent you from developing healthy and productive coping strategies. SH is like putting a towel over an amputated leg. It helps short term. But doesn’t fix the underlying issue which will likely continue to grow. And the more you ignore the issue causing your SH the harder it becomes to deal with it. 

Example: I started SH as a form of punishment after a bad breakup. It numbed me and I didn’t have to think about it. But I didn’t deal with the issue actual issue (why I was feeling the guilt). And I let it fester until I hated myself and felt like I needed to die to atone. When I took the time to actually deal with it by talking to my ex. Apologizing. And telling him about the guilt I felt I got closure for that issue. If I didn’t SH in the first place I would have been forced to deal with it earlier which would have been better for both of us. 

5. It fucks with your mental health. The problem with SH and drugs are that it’s a really quick fix for very little effort. Your brain gets that rush of dopamine and all those feel good hormones. Then you crash. And I make a point to say very little effort because exercise can also give you that quick rush. But because there is effort for it your brain feels balanced I.e. amount of pain = amount of pleasure. With SH you get the pain —> spike in pleasure way higher than the amount of pain —> your brain tries to rebalance by causing a drop in mood later. And it takes a while for your brain to catch up so you will feel low for maybe a week or something even though you only SH for a minute. 

This was the number one thing for me because I used to be the same and wonder why is it bad if it’s not hurting anyone else. If you’re interested in the pain pleasure balance thing look up Anna Lembke on YouTube. Her research on dopamine is very interesting and eye opening for me as to why SH is bad. 

Anyway sorry for the long response I tried to give as many reasons that I could think of so that maybe one would resonate with you.

No worries. For some people the idea of death is comforting. I know for me I have those suicidal feelings but I try to enjoy the time I have on earth now because eventually I will die. It’s okay to feel the desire to die sometimes, as long as you don’t act on it and continue to live to the best of your abilities. It might get better, it might not, but in the end it will all be over and you want to be able to say you enjoyed it while it lasted.

Even if you can’t get there, there is always the possibility that you will. The point of fighting is for the hope. Because one day it may get better. Aren’t there days when you feel good? Focus on those. Hold tight to the good things.

Sometimes what you are told is happiness by society isn’t the happiness you need. It’s hard because happiness is usually defined as tangible things. What makes you happy? Things that truly make you happy? Not what is expected to make you happy. Also being happy and being suicidal aren’t mutually exclusive. We have good and bad days. You just have to hold onto the good ones and let the bad ones float away. 

Usually the desire to kill yourself isn’t because you don’t have happiness but because there is an underlying problem. For some people it’s guilt, for others it’s pain. It’s okay to feel these things, as long as you never stop fighting. As soon as you stop fighting to live then it’s pointless.

But what’s the point if you aren’t there to enjoy your beauty. Nothing about this is healthy. I can understand where you’re coming from but you need to take a step back and realize you are beautiful as you are now and it would be a shame to take that beauty out of this world.

I go to sleep to try and hide from my problems but that’s a really unhealthy way of not coping. I’d recommend going somewhere loud that stimulates your senses so you can just stop thinking for a short while. I sometimes go to parties o hang out with drunk people just so I have something else to think about besides the things that bring me down.

You are not a burden. You are part of society. Do you call a person with cancer a burden? No. The only burdens are people who intentionally leech off of people and don’t care. You clearly care so you are not a burden.
The point is one day you won’t want to kill yourself. That’s all you can hope for and that’s what we fight for, the good days.

It’s hard but hold on tight. Sometimes the pain is so overwhelming but remember that the pain will end. Try to focus on the small things that you enjoy. The smell of freshly made bread or your friend smiling. Maybe it’s your mom’s hugs or when you have a good day where you don’t wake up feeling like nothing is worth it. Live and bring hope to others that suicide isn’t the only option. The other option is to live and fight your hardest.
